after.title: The classical ordered source contracts to the current algebra
after.statement: At every numerical level, the exact classical ordered augmentation has a continuous right-\(A_0\)-linear strong deformation retraction onto \(A_0\). hypotheses: The carrier is \(\varprojlim_R\operatorname*{colim}_L(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}((G_0/J_L)^n,A_0)\otimes_{\mathbb C,\mathrm{alg}}(A_0)_R)\). No uniform PBW word bound is imposed on completed left values.
The cochain homotopy is the negative of the homological matching homotopy. No projective or cofibrant claim in an unspecified topological category follows.

after.statement: At every numerical \(K\), the actual augmentation \(\epsilon:\mathcal R=N[1]\to A\) of the ordered native source has a continuous \(R_3\)-linear strong deformation retraction. It is therefore a dg bimodule quasi-isomorphism on underlying cohomology, compatibly with reduction to \(R_2\) and \(R_1\).
hypotheses: Four colours and all trace modes are retained over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), with exact RTT-pullback module quotients and the stated ordered topology.

One whole-series Laurent bound, middle cutoff and finite right support are retained at each required slice. This source is different from the original failed finite-word endpoint tensor.

after.statement: The all-exterior Cartan operators and resolved differential exist on the ordered finite-word coefficient envelope, and \(\kappa\) gives an actual continuous frame square into the global marked target. The cone-to-normalized-source quotient \(q_{\rm rel}:\mathscr D_P^{\rm rel,ord}\to\mathscr D_P^{\rm ord}\), \(q_{\rm rel}(v,w)=Qv\), has contractible kernel \(\operatorname{Cone}(\mathrm{id}_{I_P})\). after.statement: An explicit normalized homogeneous trace cochain in the original \(W_{\rightarrow}^{0,2}\) satisfies both actual Ward identities. hypotheses: Four colours and all trace modes are retained over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), with exact RTT-pullback module quotients and the stated ordered topology.
Every numerical level, through \(R_3\) on finite coefficients. The obstruction retains the original source and target bounds; it does not rule out all alternative transpose domains.

after.title: Actual native dg inputs have finite graded right duals
after.statement: For every numerical \(K\) over \(R_2\), the transported windows \(U_a^F=F(U_a^0)\) are finite free dg inputs with a strict level-zero loop action, genuine graded right evaluation and coevaluation, and the finite inverse-antipode comparison. The full Hom differential and the frame square are retained.
hypotheses: The windows are exhaustive algebraic native inputs. They lie in underlying weights at most \(a+1\); translation lands in \(U_{a+1}^F\), requiring underlying weights at most \(a+2\).
Output/source consequences are linear chain maps on literal \(R_3/\hbar^2R_3\) quotient complexes. A strict transported input action does not supply a strict output or rooted action.
For a pure current state, \(Fv=v+\frac12\hbar(K+2)T_V^\circ v\); the trace-free translation changes the scalar comparison and cannot be discarded.

after.title: The coefficient source carries the actual native state differential
after.statement: The pointwise Hom coefficient source on the actual native state complex has the all-source Cartan frame, literal \(\kappa/\Gamma\) square, full unit-relative map and compatible enlarged-stage finite-input diagram through \(R_3\). Restriction along the prescribed \(j_\hbar:B\to M\) is dg and degreewise surjective, with kernel \(\operatorname{Hom}(M/j_\hbar B,K[1])[-1]\).
hypotheses: Four colours and all trace modes are retained over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), with exact RTT-pullback module quotients and the stated ordered topology.
Every numerical level for the source maps; optional marked evaluation only at fixed \(K\ne-2\). Each algebraic input has finite word support, but its bound may vary with the input.
The graded section retains its differential defect; the restriction kernel is not asserted acyclic. Differential and translation use enlarged windows, not frozen native weight quotients.
The separate derived \(j_\hbar\) action comparison remains conditional. It is unnecessary for the established source and restriction statements.

after.title: A fixed Verma source has finite extension support
after.statement: For every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) and shifted level \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), a fixed horizontal affine Verma has nonzero actual smooth Ext to only finitely many target-weight and nonnegative-energy pairs, with a finite source-dependent degree bound. At every real \(s>0\), a uniform bound over its targets is \(\dim\mathfrak b+\lfloor\|\operatorname{Re}\lambda+\rho\|^2/(2s)\rfloor\).
hypotheses: Both homogeneous graded and actual ungraded smooth module Ext are included. The source highest weight is arbitrary complex; the degree bound need not be uniform as that source varies.
These are necessary support conditions, not assertions that every allowed Ext group is nonzero.

after.title: The changing-Verma positive-shift telescope vanishes
after.statement: Under the native hypotheses, every countable telescope of the perfect Verma preimages with strictly increasing total cohomological shifts is zero for \(s\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q_{\le0}\), allowing varying highest weights, arbitrary internal shifts and arbitrary successive maps.
hypotheses: The Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) is nonzero, finite-dimensional, simple and complex. The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.

The native transfer also assumes the actual unit and full smooth/algebraic comparison on the common-lower-energy subcategories; these hypotheses are not replaced by an arbitrary unbounded Hom formula.
Both grading conventions are included, without a common energy bound. This is a theorem about this telescope class, not a global-unit argument.

after.title: Verma-generated objects miss the regular horizontal top
after.statement: At every level, the localizing category generated by affine Vermas is a proper subcategory of \(\operatorname{Loc}(W)\) in the ungraded convention. In the graded convention all internal shifts are included on both sides: \(\operatorname{Loc}\{M_\lambda\langle a\rangle\}\subsetneq\operatorname{Loc}\{W\langle a\rangle:a\in\mathbb Z\}\). Cartan-local finiteness persists throughout the Verma-generated category, whereas the regular \(U(\mathfrak g)\) top of \(W\) violates it.
hypotheses: The Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) is nonzero, finite-dimensional, simple and complex. The recipient assertion is representation-theoretic, in graded and ungraded conventions. The separate line-source consequence requires the native tensor comparison.

after.title: Every unbounded smooth complex has an explicit injective replacement
after.statement: An actual acyclic-monomorphism cell construction iterated through \(\omega_1\) gives a strict ordinary functor \(J\) and a natural monomorphic quasi-isomorphism \(M\to J(M)\). Every term of \(J(M)\) is injective and the whole complex is K-injective, so full \(\operatorname{Hom}_A(X,J(M))\) computes ordinary smooth derived Hom for arbitrary unbounded \(X,M\).
hypotheses: Graded and ungraded smooth categories use their actual Hom conventions. The replacement functor is ordinary, not asserted dg-enriched.
Under the separate native inputs, the fixed strict right-module model supplies the native Hom action and signed unit; applying \(J\) alone does not create that action.

after.title: The ordinary unit fails at every integral affine level at most minus four
after.statement: For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) at raw affine level \(-p-2\), \(p\ge2\), a telescope of perfect Verma preimages gives \(L_p\ne0\) with \(\Phi_pL_p=0\). The actual ordinary unit is \(L_p\to0\), with nonzero cone \(L_p[1]\). An infinite-projection map entirely within the generated recipient also proves that \(W_p\) is not compact there.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.

The native transfer also assumes the actual unit and full smooth/algebraic comparison on the common-lower-energy subcategories; these hypotheses are not replaced by an arbitrary unbounded Hom formula.

Ordinary unbounded derived categories with ordinary coefficient quasi-isomorphisms; internal weights are algebraic sums of arbitrary support. No cohomological, common energy or finite-dimensionality bound is imposed.

The actual normalized Ext-one classes have every finite initial Yoneda product nonzero. The conclusions hold graded and ungraded. The family does not cover shifted level \(-1\) or negative nonintegral rational levels.

after.title: Every simple type has a noncritical unit kernel at a specified level
after.statement: For every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) at raw affine level \(-2h^\vee\), an explicit affine-Weyl ascent chain gives an ordinary line telescope \(L\ne0\) with \(\Phi L=0\). Its actual unit has cone \(L[1]\ne0\). The same construction proves failure of compactness of \(W\) within its own localizing image.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.

The native transfer also assumes the actual unit and full smooth/algebraic comparison on the common-lower-energy subcategories; these hypotheses are not replaced by an arbitrary unbounded Hom formula.

Ordinary unbounded derived categories with ordinary coefficient quasi-isomorphisms; internal weights are algebraic sums of arbitrary support. No cohomological, common energy or finite-dimensionality bound is imposed.
This is one specified noncritical level in every simple type, including nonsimplylaced types. It uses same-type extension products, and does not assert failure at every noncritical level.

after.title: The regular top has disjoint positive-weight central supports
after.statement: For affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), \(s=\ell+2\ne0\), positive-weight smooth self-Ext of \(W\) has \(\Omega_L-\Omega_R=2sw\) and right annihilator \(Q_w(T)=\prod_{m=1}^w[(2sw-2m^2)^2-4m^2(2T+1)]\). At \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), all positive-weight left supports are disjoint from all positive-weight right supports; the resulting module-level Tor groups vanish.
hypotheses: The actual regular \(U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)\) top and its source-precomposition/target-postcomposition actions are used. Fixed-weight amplitude is finite; no common all-weight amplitude bound is asserted.
This representation-theoretic theorem requires no native adjunction. Passing to the actual native ideal is a separate derived theorem.

after.title: A derived square-zero ideal reduces every source to two inflated complexes
after.statement: Let \(B\to R\) be a split augmented dg algebra, K-flat over \(R\) on both sides, with ideal \(I\) satisfying \(I\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}I=0\). For \(F=R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-\), inflation \(U\), and \(J=R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}I\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}R\), every unbounded \(L\) has a natural triangle \(U(J\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F(L))\to L\to UF(L)\). For any exact adjunction out of \(D(B)\), its actual unit is globally invertible exactly when it is invertible on every inflated \(R\)-complex.
hypotheses: Ordinary algebraic direct sums and unbounded derived tensors are used, in either grading convention. The middle arrow is the actual extension-of-scalars unit.
Derived tensor vanishing is stronger than square-zero multiplication. No unrestricted coproduct preservation by a right adjoint is assumed.

after.title: The actual nonrational rank-one ideal has zero derived tensor square
after.statement: For \(B=Y_{-s}\), \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), the actual positive-weight ideal \(I=\bigoplus_{w>0}B_w\) satisfies \(I\otimes_{U(\mathfrak{sl}_2)}^{\mathbf L}I\simeq0\), retaining both outer actions in the graded and ungraded bimodule categories.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.
The exact supported graded unit on the free object \(B\) and the prescribed strict smooth right-module model are retained inputs.
The supported generator unit identifies the correctly oriented native bimodule structure. Finite-weight derived annihilator powers and algebraic coproducts establish the full ideal assertion.

after.title: Restricted positive-current cofree modules are genuinely injective
after.statement: For \(\mathfrak n=t\mathfrak{sl}_2[t]\) over \(\mathbb C\) or \(\mathbb C((q))\), its restricted finite-energy cofree module \(C\) has \(C\otimes T\) injective in the actual smooth positive-current category for every coefficient vector space \(T\). The assertion also holds in the algebraically graded category with arbitrary coefficient-weight support.
hypotheses: The current action is on \(C\) alone and every element has finite cofree support. This is not affine injectivity, a restricted affine-coinduction adjunction, or by itself an arbitrary-complex K-injectivity assertion.

after.title: The actual unit is invertible on every inflated base complex
after.statement: For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), native \(k\notin\mathbb Q\) and raw affine level \(\ell=-k-2\), the actual native unit is an equivalence on every ordinary unbounded complex inflated from the full ghost quotient \(H=U(\mathfrak g[t^{-1}])\), hence from \(R=U(\mathfrak g)\). The signed unit evaluates at the vacuum to the identity under the genuine unbounded Shapiro comparison.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.

Ordinary unbounded derived categories with ordinary coefficient quasi-isomorphisms; internal weights are algebraic sums of arbitrary support. No cohomological, common energy or finite-dimensionality bound is imposed.

The cofree factor remains an algebraic sum. The proof uses the fixed coherent smooth right-module model and positive-current injectivity, without extending a bounded cochain formula to arbitrary inputs.

after.title: Nonrational rank-one induction is fully faithful on the entire ordinary source
after.statement: For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\), native \(k\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q\) and raw affine level \(\ell=-k-2\), the actual unit \(L\to\Psi\Phi L\) is an equivalence for every ordinary unbounded \(Y_k\)-module, including nonzero ghost actions. The actual realization is fully faithful with image exactly \(\operatorname{Loc}(W)\), or \(\operatorname{Loc}\{W\langle w\rangle:w\in\mathbb Z\}\) in the graded convention.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.

Ordinary unbounded derived categories with ordinary coefficient quasi-isomorphisms; internal weights are algebraic sums of arbitrary support. No cohomological, common energy or finite-dimensionality bound is imposed.

The derived native ideal theorem, the full-domain reduction and the actual all-inflated unit are combined with their exact maps. The image is not asserted to be every smooth object or every object with torsion cohomology.

after.title: The actual counit is the cellular approximation at nonrational rank one
after.statement: Under the same nonrational \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) native hypotheses, \(W\) and its required internal shifts are compact within the generated image. For every unrestricted smooth target \(M\), the actual counit \(\Phi\Psi M\to M\) is canonically the cellular-coreflector map \(\operatorname{Cell}_W M\to M\); it is invertible exactly on that image.
hypotheses: The prescribed coherent native right action, actual smooth tensor–Hom adjunction, exact affine-free lifts and cutoff compatibility remain hypotheses. The graded and ungraded native realizations are supplied separately.
The exact supported graded unit on the free object \(B\) and the prescribed strict smooth right-module model are retained inputs.

Ordinary unbounded derived categories with ordinary coefficient quasi-isomorphisms; internal weights are algebraic sums of arbitrary support. No cohomological, common energy or finite-dimensionality bound is imposed.

Compactness is relative to the localizing image, not to the entire smooth derived category. The positive-weight ideal in the line algebra differs from the positive-current augmentation ideal used for cellularization.

after.title: One nilpotent current has an exact unbounded torsion comparison
after.statement: For \(x=at\) with nonzero ad-nilpotent \(a\), smooth Ore localization \(L_x\) is exact and \(i_xR\Gamma_xM\simeq\operatorname{fib}(M\to L_xM)\) on every ordinary unbounded smooth complex. The inclusion of the derived \(x\)-torsion category is fully faithful, with exactly \(x\)-torsion cohomology as image.
hypotheses: Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and every affine level, graded and ungraded. No native adjunction hypothesis is needed.

after.title: A finite nilpotent basis detects joint torsion
after.statement: A nilpotent basis \(a_i\) of \(\mathfrak g\), with \(x_i=a_it\), gives \(\mathcal T_I=\bigcap_i\ker L_{x_i}\) and \(D_I=\bigcap_i\ker DL_{x_i}\). These exact detectors characterize joint torsion and its cohomological category.
hypotheses: Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and every affine level. These equalities do not identify the intrinsic derived torsion category with its ambient cohomological category.

after.title: The single-current localizations do not preserve each other’s torsion
after.statement: At every affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) level, an explicit smooth module is \(ft\)-torsion while its localization at \(et\) is not. Thus iterating the single-current detectors is not automatically a construction of joint derived torsion.
hypotheses: The graded and ungraded examples are actual smooth affine modules. This obstruction to a chosen construction does not refute the joint comparison.

after.title: Positive-current torsion is stable under injective envelopes
after.statement: The smooth positive-current category is locally noetherian, and joint augmentation torsion is stable under injective envelopes. Finite nilpotent Rees algebras and the resulting Artin–Rees statement give the actual stability theorem on every smooth cyclic module.
hypotheses: Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra. Affine injective stability is not inferred merely by restriction.

after.title: Actual derived torsion commutes with positive-current restriction
after.statement: Exact induction on the smooth and torsion categories yields \(\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal T}R\Gamma_A\simeq R\Gamma_{\mathfrak n}\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal S}\) on every ordinary unbounded complex, with the actual units and counits. Restriction is conservative; every torsion affine module is \(\Gamma_A\)-acyclic, so \(\Gamma_A\) is weakly stable.
hypotheses: Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra and every affine level. The derived functors use genuine K-injective replacements; no unrestricted continuous-cochain model is substituted.

after.title: Positive-current derived torsion has infinite cohomological dimension
after.statement: For \(R_N=U(\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n_N)\) with its inflated regular action, the first nonzero derived torsion lies in degree \(d_N=(N-1)\dim\mathfrak g\). Its invariant line has energy \(\Delta_N=\dim(\mathfrak g)N(N-1)/2\). These degrees are unbounded.
hypotheses: This is an actual smooth positive-current calculation for every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra. Infinite cohomological dimension alone does not decide the joint derived embedding.

after.title: Positive-current derived torsion fails to preserve a countable coproduct
after.statement: For the shifted regular quotients \(R_N[d_N]\), the actual comparison \(\bigoplus_N R\Gamma(R_N[d_N])\to R\Gamma(\bigoplus_N R_N[d_N])\) has a nonzero degree-zero defect containing \(\mathbb C^{\mathbb N}/\mathbb C^{(\mathbb N)}\). An actual acyclic complex of injectives \(K\) realizes the defect: \(R\Gamma K=0\) but termwise \(\Gamma K\) is not acyclic.
hypotheses: Every nonzero finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra in the ordinary smooth positive-current category. In the algebraically graded version, the individual shift \(\langle-\Delta_N\rangle\) places all diagonal classes in energy zero.

The proof uses genuine K-injective products and the actual comparison map. It does not transfer an affine coproduct failure by restriction, or by itself decide the joint derived embedding or equality with cellularization.

after.title: A bare exterior E3 algebra has no coupling parameter
after.statement: A strictly unital \(E_3\)-algebra over \(\mathbb C\) with cohomology \(\Lambda(x_3)\), \(|x_3|=3\), is unique up to equivalence at the level of its bare \(E_3\) structure. That structure alone therefore supplies no varying coupling scalar. A filtration, mixed action, retained translation or central-charge class, marked comparison, or braided category is additional data.
hypotheses: This is single-generator exterior rigidity. It is not a rigidity theorem for arbitrary simple affine cohomology, and uniqueness does not construct an enhancement on a separately prescribed object.
Rank-one coefficient Koszul comparisons retain their specified unipotent sector and separate charge grading; no full all-charge braided equivalence follows from bare formality.

after.title: The critical translation cone retains kernel and cokernel data
after.statement: For the two-term translation object \(z_{\rm top}=\operatorname{fib}(T:Z\to Z)\), its cohomology fits into \(0\to\operatorname{coker}(T:H^{n-1}Z\to H^{n-1}Z)\to H^n(z_{\rm top})\to\ker(T:H^nZ\to H^nZ)\to0\). At critical level it cannot simply be identified with the oper-form cohomology of the input \(Z\).
hypotheses: This is the formal consequence of the stated translation-cone definition. It does not identify an actual universal critical action space, construct its \(E_2\) structure, or transfer a bracket.

after.title: The native polar diagram has a fifth-order obstruction problem
after.statement: Determine the actual fifth-order residual for the prescribed \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) polar comparison in diagram form over \(k[K]\), retaining its native source, lower-order maps and operation identities. The collision-only strict Hopf-twist ansatz is a separate proposal, with a proposed order-\(\hbar^2\) obstruction; neither an all-order native comparison nor uniqueness is established by that proposal. The existing all-order elliptic theorem concerns its own specified family and does not settle this diagram comparison.
hypotheses: The source and prescribed operations belong to the native diagram-form polar problem. A strict Hopf twist, published existence of other quantum vertex structures and a distinct elliptic family are not replacements for that comparison.
No new all-order theorem, uniqueness statement or universal native realization follows from this obstruction question.

after.title: Positive recipients have a functorial entire-vector core
after.statement: Every closed invariant subspace of a finite product of the specified positive recipients has a dense complete Fréchet space of vectors entire for the energy action. Its topology is defined using the actual Gaussian-growth final or spectral strong topology. Gaussian Fourier smoothing and the local meromorphic germs are actual continuous operations. Every continuous linear Virasoro morphism preserves these cores with one uniform energy shift, independently of the finite-product presentation.
hypotheses: Fix real \(c>1\). The objects are closed invariant subspaces of finite products of the Gaussian-growth section recipient and admitted positive spectral strong duals; no arbitrary product or nonpositive factor is included.

after.title: The functorial positive core is not preserved by collision
after.statement: The actual primary binary collision lies outside the positive entire-vector cores even after every finite complex energy propagation, for the canonical spectral measure and the explicitly admitted alternative measures. Gaussian smoothing changes that operation and is not a Virasoro intertwiner. Separate actual weak-meromorphic and vacuum graph-dual examples also prevent the unchanged ordinary-energy smoothing construction on those factors.
hypotheses: Real \(c>1\), the original normalized positive vertices and canonical measure, boundary hypothesis \(H\), and the stated analytic estimates are retained. Tree comparisons also retain the normalized positive-label pentagon.

For another scalar measure \(\nu\), the collision must have its actual scalar-multiplicity-one realization and satisfy \(\int_0^\infty e^{\delta h(p)}d\nu(p)=\infty\) for every \(\delta>0\). The canonical measure satisfies this condition.

For the Gaussian multiplier \(e^{-\varepsilon L_0^2}\), the specified weak-meromorphic example fails every ordinary exponential stage for all \(\varepsilon>0\); the actual vacuum graph-dual example asserts that failure for \(0<\varepsilon<1\). No assertion for its vacuum case at \(\varepsilon\ge1\) is made.

after.title: Every finite positive radial comb has its natural output range
after.statement: For every fixed finite number \(d\ge2\) of positive inputs, the actual radial comb exists on \(0<|a_2|<\cdots<|a_d|\) in every strict output stage \(s<-\log|a_d|\). Each compact coordinate set admits one finite Hilbert input stage with a Hilbert–Schmidt bound uniform in all original positive labels and locally uniform in charge. The complete entangled source is \(\widehat\bigotimes_{i=1}^d{}_{\pi}\mathscr E_{p_i}\). All internal and final labels and all descendant levels are uncut, with normally convergent actual cutoffs and exact mark \(2^{(d-1)/4}\sqrt{\prod_v C_0}\).
hypotheses: Real \(c>1\), the original normalized positive vertices and canonical measure, boundary hypothesis \(H\), and the stated analytic estimates are retained. Tree comparisons also retain the normalized positive-label pentagon.
Coordinates have fixed logarithmic branches. Constants and source stages may depend on the finite word and the coordinate compact.

after.title: Three positive inputs have an actual vacuum-output sewing
after.statement: For fixed positive labels \(A,B,C\), the fixed-\(C\) positive point vertex followed by the coefficient-one vacuum cap defines \(\Theta_z:\mathscr E_A\widehat\otimes_\pi\mathscr E_B\widehat\otimes_\pi\mathscr E_C\to G'_b\) on \(0<|z|<1/2\). It is holomorphic with locally common finite input stages, normally convergent intermediate and vacuum expansions, and the full rational Ward identities on all entangled inputs. All continuous linear Ward maps from this source to \(G'_b\) form exactly \(\mathbb C\Theta_z\). Its single positive binary mark is \(2^{1/4}\sqrt{C_0(A,B,C)}\).
hypotheses: Real \(c>1\), the original normalized positive vertices and canonical measure, boundary hypothesis \(H\), and the stated analytic estimates are retained. Tree comparisons also retain the normalized positive-label pentagon.

The output is the complex-linear strong dual of the original vacuum graph \(G=V_\sigma^{\mathrm W}\). The intermediate positive module is the fixed module \(C\); this is not point evaluation of an arbitrary spectral \(L^2\) section.

after.title: The common three-input carrier represents the vacuum target
after.statement: The actual positive sewing \(Q_z\) and vacuum map \(\Theta_z\) have the complete invariant joint image closure \(R_z^{+,V}=\overline{(Q_z,\Theta_z)(E_{ABC})}\) in the product of their original strong-dual recipients. The vacuum projection induces \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Vir,cont}}(R_z^{+,V},G'_b)\cong\operatorname{Ward}^{G'}_{ABC}(z)=\mathbb C\Theta_z\). A closed finite positive-product recipient has a continuous inverse to \(L_0\) and no nonzero continuous Virasoro map to \(G'_b\); its positive component alone cannot represent this nonzero vacuum output. The exact quotient source maps continuously, injectively and densely into the joint closure.
hypotheses: Real \(c>1\), the original normalized positive vertices and canonical measure, boundary hypothesis \(H\), and the stated analytic estimates are retained. Tree comparisons also retain the normalized positive-label pentagon.

Initially \(0<|z|<1/2\), fixed positive labels and the completed three-input source. The joint closure uses the actual product topology; no embedding or inverse topology is asserted for its quotient source.

after.title: The three-input vacuum output reaches the full real interior
after.statement: The same three-positive-input vacuum map extends to the complex lens \(\mathcal L=\{|z|<1,\ |1-z|<1\}\), which contains every real \(0<z<1\). An actual Möbius transport supplies the fixed Hilbert-dual realization \(V_\sigma'\), locally common finite input stages and the unchanged graph dual. Its phase \(e^{-i\pi(h_A+h_C)}\) preserves the primary coefficient \(2^{1/4}\sqrt{C_0(A,B,C)}z^{h_C-h_A-h_B}(1-z)^{h_A-h_B-h_C}\). The full Ward identities, the one-dimensional vacuum-target classification and the joint-carrier projection hold throughout this lens.
hypotheses: Real \(c>1\), the original normalized positive vertices and canonical measure, boundary hypothesis \(H\), and the stated analytic estimates are retained. Tree comparisons also retain the normalized positive-label pentagon.
The branches of \(\log z\) and \(\log(1-z)\) are real on the ordered interval. The original vacuum source and normalization are unchanged.

after.title: Independent finite trees have coherent actual comparisons
after.statement: Every finite positive planar binary tree has an independently constructed normal sewing corner with full entangled Hilbert bounds and uncut spectra. Each elementary rotation is identified on an actual common sewing domain by the normalized positive-affine four-point unitary. The square and pentagon identities make every finite reassociation path depend only on its endpoints. The resulting unitary identifies the continuation of each independent germ with the radial comb on its logarithmic radial domain; a noncomb raw series is asserted only on its own connected normal sewing domains.
hypotheses: Real \(c>1\), the original normalized positive vertices and canonical measure, boundary hypothesis \(H\), and the stated analytic estimates are retained. Tree comparisons also retain the normalized positive-label pentagon.
Every internal label remains a resolved multiplicity. Local exponents and translation stages satisfy their strict vertex inequalities; no seam is applied to an arbitrary distributional recipient.

after.title: Finite sewings have complete Ward recipients and quotient sources
after.statement: Every admitted finite positive sewing and its identified continuation satisfies the full rational Ward identities on the complete entangled source. Its tree-independent kernel defines a complete Fréchet quotient, continuously and densely injected into the complete invariant image closure. Every admitted intermediate forest gives a continuous open quotient sewing, and finite successive quotient sewings agree. This uses actual packets at the stages received by their parent vertices. Representing a general continuous linear composite Ward map still requires both kernel annihilation and continuity in the topology induced from the recipient, not merely the finer quotient-source topology.
hypotheses: Real \(c>1\), the original normalized positive vertices and canonical measure, boundary hypothesis \(H\), and the stated analytic estimates are retained. Tree comparisons also retain the normalized positive-label pentagon.
Forest sewings use the stated completed projective tensor sources and actual inner packet domains. The binary common tuple may be used at an innermost pair through its exact canonical packet kernel.

after.title: One vacuum input is controlled in every finite word
after.statement: With the original graph source \(G\) and any fixed finite number \(r\ge1\) of positive inputs, the full entangled graph-array source is its completed projective tensor source. A nonfirst vacuum admits every strict natural output exponent \(s<-\log|a_{r+1}|\) in the actual forward comb. A first vacuum is independently realized by reflection into \(Z[-b]\) for every fixed \(b>\log2\) on the normalized real interior. Every mixed tree has its own normal corner, full rational Ward covariance and coherent comparisons induced by the pruned positive tree. Vacuum insertion has coefficient one, including the actual left translation. Mixed and pruned-positive image closures agree in the same ambient topology, while the corresponding positive-to-mixed source map is asserted only to be a continuous injection.
hypotheses: Real \(c>1\), the original normalized positive vertices and canonical measure, boundary hypothesis \(H\), and the stated analytic estimates are retained. Tree comparisons also retain the normalized positive-label pentagon.
The mark is \(2^{(r-1)/4}\sqrt{\prod C_0}\), with coefficient one at the vacuum vertex. The original \(G\) is unchanged; reflected and translated maps retain their actual stage bounds.

after.title: Original spectral inputs can be retained through finite sewing
after.statement: Arbitrary positive original spectral measures in standard separable realizations, with measurable separable Hilbert multiplicities, admit bounded holomorphic finite-word sewing on the full entangled entire-energy Hilbert-array source. Every original spectral variable remains an output multiplicity; only new internal and final labels use the canonical measure. The fixed-label comparisons, full Ward identities and finite coherence survive direct integration, including one vacuum input. Cutoffs converge on each input locally uniformly: raw contractions are used on their own normal domains, and constant comparison operators transport comb approximants elsewhere. No global Hilbert–Schmidt bound is claimed over an atomless original measure.
hypotheses: Real \(c>1\), the original normalized positive vertices and canonical measure, boundary hypothesis \(H\), and the stated analytic estimates are retained. Tree comparisons also retain the normalized positive-label pentagon.
Use a sigma-finite realization or equivalent finite scalar control measure. Original input measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the canonical measure.

after.title: The supported-partner matrix includes every finite fresh jet
after.statement: The supported-partner map \(\mathcal R_q=\rho_q^{-1}g_q^{\mathrm{nat}}(C\,\cdot)\), \(C=(4\pi^2)^{-1}\), is evaluated on every finite fresh incoming \(\sigma\) degree and all four contact-exterior rows of its actual supported carrier. The fresh power contributes \((-t(\partial_x-\zeta))^\gamma\) in the finite polynomial integral, with outgoing contact jet \(\zeta\); the physical incoming variable \(S=\sigma-\alpha\) instead contributes \((-\alpha-t(\partial_x-\zeta))^\gamma\). The full coefficient boundary, finite-stage bounds and specified normal, coordinate and old-face squares remain. The top exterior row kills positive incoming fresh degree instead of turning it into an outgoing contact jet.
hypotheses: Use the original labelled matching with roots \(U,U,V\), the prescribed current quotient, finite normal and physical jets, coefficient differential, anchor and suspension signs, determinant and excess factors, and separately retained central and elliptic outputs.

The carrier contains finite jets of \(c_Uc_h\), prescribed ordered one-edge \(x\)-current actions, their differentials and supported descendants, finite auxiliary polynomials and allowed smooth spectator stages.

after.title: Fourth-order point currents have explicit central prisms
after.statement: The original full central de Rham contraction gives finite primitives and branch comparisons for the available trace-zero point currents of total derivative order at most four. Its inverse tensor constraint defines the universal top map into the stated output, and its coend product retains the prescribed inverse block crossing.
The output is one fused module. This coend does not represent every family in the enlarged Gaussian or mixed category.

after.title: The intrinsic balanced operations form a proper ambient subsystem
after.statement: The marked \(W\)-balanced operation subsystem is not closed under arbitrary ambient horizontal postcomposition. The vacuum projection gives a counterexample even in charge zero. Thus the faithful intrinsic embedding does not identify all ambient mixed \(\operatorname{Hom}\) spaces or reconstruct the whole enlarged category from its finite KZ coend.
hypotheses: The source balance, vacuum normalization and fixed actual comparisons are retained.
Generated every-context-compatible maps remain admitted; arbitrary intermediate-channel projectors, block splittings and unrestricted completions require separate hypotheses.

after.title: Local cyclic Riesz spaces carry actual based action Gaussians
after.statement: Every specified finite cyclic Riesz space has a convergent even Gaussian cycle and ordered odd integral, with its independently based semidensity. With the independently chosen current determinant semidensity frames, the actual affine-to-stress/quartet change of variables gives finite Fubini with \(J_\Gamma=\varepsilon_\Gamma j_\Gamma\), where \(j_\Gamma\) is the inverse current Berezinian and \(\varepsilon_\Gamma\in\{\pm1\}\) is the separate cycle comparison.
hypotheses: Fix \(0<|q|<1\), \(\kappa\ne0\), \(\hbar>0\), the local cyclic gauge and its exact paired carriers.
Fix each Riesz contour and shrink to a constant-rank source patch; smooth or holomorphic dependence follows the actual finite data.

Choose the three homogeneous current frames independently and use their inverse determinant sections as semidensities, with stress before quartet in the determinant order. Finite stress rescaling, odd order and even-cycle phases are specified before integration. For arbitrary input density factors the density Jacobian instead retains \([\rho_{\mathrm{aff}}/(\rho_{\mathrm{st}}\rho_{\mathcal Q})]\operatorname{Ber}_{L}(m)^{-1}\), where the \(\rho\)'s are the three chosen density factors and \(m\) is the finite Lagrangian change of variables.
These Riesz action spaces are not identified with the original coefficient-cutoff integration spaces.

after.title: The local quartet has a computed finite phase and a retained harmonic state
after.statement: On each complete paired spectral cut, the signed singular-frame quartet integral is \(1\), while the literal-frame integral is \((-1)^{N_\Sigma+\eta_\Sigma}\). The full mass-one harmonic residual remains an eight-dimensional paired state with its internal differential; its signed integral is \(+1\) and its literal integral is \(-1\).
hypotheses: \(N_\Sigma\) counts positive coefficient singular pairs and \(\eta_\Sigma=1\) when the full mass-one block is included.
Use the specified coefficient metrics, actual finite action, real even cycle, ordered odd extraction and frame convention.
An unscaled sequence of literal signs converges only when its prescribed parity is eventually constant. Positive heat torsion alone does not establish that condition.

after.title: The local gauge has an intrinsic heat source connection and finite part
after.statement: On the new paired local-gauge carriers, positive-time action heat has its full weak source insertion and equals the direct coefficient endpoint heat torsion. Local bulk and boundary counterterms give an intrinsic finite part in \(C^k\), with \(O(\sqrt\epsilon)\) remainder and commutation with the prescribed finite source derivatives.
hypotheses: Use a finite-dimensional \(C^k\) family of sufficiently small smooth reflected Ward sources, with finitely many sufficiently high smooth bounds and the stated radial metrics.
The exact paired-dual weak boundary distribution and the moving native source-graph Green contact remain in source differentiation.
The finite-part prescription belongs to this local gauge. Identification with original coefficient-cutoff semidensities, physical action corrections or an absolute continuum phase remains separate.

after.title: Actual finite shell integrals glue a local Gaussian line
after.statement: Finite cyclic shell integration glues the local spectral charts to a Gaussian line with transition \(T_{ij}=g_j/g_i\). The graded Kato determinant connection is flat, and the actual affine density factor is source-constant in its independently parallel current frames. The full Kato connection can still have nonzero curvature.
hypotheses: Use the fixed local/Riesz carrier, actual internally invariant current projections, small reflected Ward sources and finitely many contours on each overlap.

On the finite paired cyclic Riesz space \(F_\Gamma\), let \(H_\Gamma\) be the paired heat generator and \(N\) total degree. Set \(k_\Gamma=\tfrac12\operatorname{Str}_{F_\Gamma}(N\log H_\Gamma)\), using the logarithm on the fixed right half-plane. In a parallel density-cycle frame, the actual action integral is \(g_\Gamma=c_\Gamma e^{k_\Gamma}\), with \(c_\Gamma=g_\Gamma(u_*)e^{-k_\Gamma(u_*)}\ne0\) at a chosen reference source \(u_*\). Every action constant, frame factor, quartet sign and cycle phase stays in \(c_\Gamma\).
No source neighborhood common to an unbounded family of contours, convergence of arbitrary independently based bare vacua or infinite literal phase product is asserted.

after.title: A finite action anchor determines a horizontal renormalized section
after.statement: An independently specified nonzero finite action anchor determines a section of the glued local Gaussian line. Its complementary heat finite part is \(h_{\mathrm{ren}}-k_\Gamma-\gamma_E\nu_\Gamma\); the finite action constants and Euler term give exact gluing. After counterterm scaling, sections converge in \(C^k\) and source connections in \(C^{k-1}\). Actual affine Fubini descends and preserves these transports.
hypotheses: Use a contractible finite-dimensional \(C^k\) source chart, \(k\ge2\), of sufficiently small smooth reflected Ward pairs, containing source zero. Its prescribed finite source jets are bounded in sufficiently many coefficient norms, on the fixed marked geometry and nonzero level.

For the finite paired cyclic Riesz space \(F_\Gamma\), \(N\) is total degree and \(H_\Gamma\) is its paired heat generator. Define \(\nu_\Gamma=\tfrac12\operatorname{Str}_{F_\Gamma}N\) and \(k_\Gamma=\tfrac12\operatorname{Str}_{F_\Gamma}(N\log H_\Gamma)\), with the logarithm on the fixed right half-plane. Here \(\gamma_E\) is Euler's constant, and \(h_{\mathrm{ren}}\) is the intrinsic local coefficient heat finite part after its specified local subtractions.

The finite anchor includes its own scalar and phase, and the quartet vacuum is counted once. In a parallel density-cycle frame, \(g_\Gamma=c_\Gamma e^{k_\Gamma}\) is the actual action integral and \(c_\Gamma\ne0\) retains its based density and cycle phase.
Positive-scale source and scale transport is exact; the stated source estimates do not give a pointwise limit of the \(d\epsilon\) component at zero.
The result is on the local/Riesz line with the exact paired boundary forms. Original cutoff, fixed-adjoint and physical-cap identifications remain additional.

after.title: The specified boundary-zero filling has zero formal native finite part
after.statement: For \(F_\lambda=z-\lambda z(t/r)^2\), the original fixed-adjoint native connection has zero heat finite part at every formal source degree. Its source derivative is \(\left.\partial_\lambda\Theta^{\mathrm{nat}}_{\epsilon,\lambda}\right|_0=A_\kappa\epsilon^{-3/2}+B_\kappa\epsilon^{-1/2}+O(\sqrt\epsilon)\), with both power coefficients retained. The independent stress connection vanishes at each positive heat time coefficientwise, and this family has exactly zero source-graph Green contact.
hypotheses: Use \(q=e^{-L}\in(0,1)\), \(L>0\), \(\kappa\ne0\), the original radial coefficient metric and full reflection realization.
The source is the full rational filling family and its Schwarzian stress; the adjoints are fixed at source zero.

Finite parts are coefficientwise in formal \(\lambda\). The \(\lambda^2\) coefficient of the source-zero-normalized scalar primitive is one half of the displayed connection derivative. Neither the native positive-time connection nor its unevaluated power coefficients is declared zero.
This is a theorem for the specified family, not general filling independence or a numerical resummed small-time theorem.

after.title: The original coefficient cutoffs have a formal positive-heat limit
after.statement: The original finite action Gaussian determines \(\mathcal G_{\Lambda,\epsilon}(\mu)=G_\Lambda(0)\exp(W_{\Lambda,\epsilon}(\mu)-W_{\Lambda,\epsilon}(0))\). At fixed positive heat time its source-normalized ratio, source connection and fixed source derivatives converge coefficientwise as the original cutoff is removed, with rapid spectral tails. At fixed finite cutoff, removing the heat recovers the original Gaussian branch.
hypotheses: Fix \(\kappa\ne0\), \(\hbar>0\), marked \(0<|q|<1\), the common coefficient metric and a fully reflected smooth integrable formal family with its actual Ward filling.

For the original cutoff coefficient complex \(C_\Lambda\), set \(a_\Lambda=d_{\Lambda,0}^{\dagger}\), \(\Delta_{\Lambda,\mu}=\{d_{\Lambda,\mu},a_\Lambda\}\) and \(W_{\Lambda,\epsilon}=-\int_\epsilon^\infty\operatorname{Str}_{C_\Lambda}(Ne^{-t\Delta_{\Lambda,\mu}})\,dt/t\). Here \(N\) is total coefficient degree including ghosts; this coefficient trace has no paired factor \(1/2\). The adjoint is fixed at source zero. Full HPL returns, mixed source jets and ordered Duhamel terms remain in every variation.
The original \(G_\Lambda(0)\), shell determinants/Pfaffians, density and phase remain. No numerical cutoff limit or joint cutoff/heat limit follows.

after.title: The formal placement difference has a local boundary factor
after.statement: The direct heat constant of the original two-placement difference is a closed local boundary one-form, determined by a finite native jet recursion. Its source-zero-normalized primitive \(C_{\mathrm{place}}\) gives the relative factor \(\exp C_{\mathrm{place}}\) after the two logarithmic potentials are renormalized in that common convention. A whole integrable family vanishing in a fixed boundary collar has \(C_{\mathrm{place}}=0\).
hypotheses: At each fixed source degree, retain the actual metric, ghost terms, distinct heat speeds, full mixed source jets and finite upper geometry.
Uniform \(O(\sqrt\epsilon)\) remainders require bounded finitely many sufficiently high \(C^K\) seminorms on the double; boundary jet values alone are insufficient.
The primitive follows the actual integrable parameter family. It is the finite part of a logarithmic potential, not the finite part of an exponential.

General boundary coefficients remain unevaluated. A zero relative phase requires the stated real \(q=e^{-L}\) family and anti-linear symmetry; the absolute source-zero phase and global holonomy remain separate.

after.title: The original fixed-adjoint expression has numerical heat on weighted coefficients
after.statement: The operator \(A_{\mu,T}=\{d_{\mu,T},a_0\}\), with the original \(a_0=d_0^\dagger\) held fixed, has a gapped sectorial realization on reflected coefficient offsets \((2,1,0,2,0)\), with common domain two Sobolev derivatives higher. On one small \(C^4(\mu)\oplus C^1(T)\) ball its heat is source-holomorphic and trace class, with \(\|e^{-tA}\|_1\le C(1+t^{-3/2})e^{-ct}\).
hypotheses: Fix the original radial metric, marked \(0<|q|<1\) and \(\kappa\ne0\), in component order \((E,H,F,b,c)\).
The common domain has regularities \((4,3,2,4,2)\) and all corresponding iterated reflection conditions, defined on the double.
The carrier changes; the differential expression \(a_0\) is not replaced by the Hilbert adjoint in the new norm.
Every fixed ambient source derivative obeys the same time exponent on smaller balls. Smooth-kernel assertions use smooth sources with the required finite higher bounds.

after.title: Smooth Ward sources have a genuine weighted coefficient contraction
after.statement: On the smooth Ward locus, the closed coefficient differential and fixed gauge have their maximal doubled distributional graph domains. The bounded map \(r=a_0A_{\mu,T}^{-1}\) satisfies \(r^2=0\) and \(dr+rd=1\) on the differential domain. It preserves the original fixed smooth gauge image and agrees with the ordinary reduced inverse on their common domain.
hypotheses: Use the numerical weighted carrier and one sufficiently small finite-norm source ball, with smooth reflected integrable sources and actual Ward stress.

In component order \((E,H,F,b,c)\), set \(\mathbf r=(2,1,0,2,0)\), \(\mathbf w=(0,1,2,0,1)\), and \(X^s=\bigoplus_iH_+^{s+r_i}(w_i)\). Here \(H_+^s(w)\) is the positive-reflection Sobolev space of weight-\(w\) coefficient forms, defined on the closed double and then restricted to the half-manifold. The graph domains contain \(X^1\) but are not identified with it; no negative-order half-manifold trace is imposed.
This contraction does not sum an original sharp-tail HPL series, construct the full paired moving-graph heat domain or overturn the original physical coefficient-\(L^2\) obstruction.

after.title: Numerical positive-time scalars realize the formal Taylor coefficients
after.statement: The source-normalized scalar \(\mathcal R_\epsilon=\exp(W_\epsilon-W_\epsilon(0,0))\), with \(W_\epsilon=-\int_\epsilon^\infty\operatorname{Str}_X(Ne^{-tA_{\mu,T}})\,dt/t\), is numerical, holomorphic and nonzero. Here \(N\) is total coefficient degree including internal ghost degrees, and \(\operatorname{Str}_X\) is the graded trace on the weighted coefficient carrier \(X\). Its complete source, scale and mixed derivatives have exactly the formal ordered Duhamel coefficients of the original-cutoff prescription. The numerical Ward-family placement identity uses the two actual heats.
hypotheses: Heat time is fixed and positive. In component order \((E,H,F,b,c)\), \(X=\bigoplus_iH_+^{r_i}(w_i)\), with \(\mathbf r=(2,1,0,2,0)\), \(\mathbf w=(0,1,2,0,1)\); \(H_+^s(w)\) denotes the positive-reflection Sobolev coefficient space on the double, restricted to the half-manifold. The heat generator is \(A_{\mu,T}=\{d_{\mu,T},d_0^\dagger\}\), with the original source-zero adjoint fixed.
Scalar algebra also holds for the polynomial source extension off the Ward locus; cochain and closed-tangent placement identities require Ward.
An arbitrary formal family is pulled back coefficientwise; convergence of its source series is not assumed.
No general numerical small-time expansion, logarithm exclusion, numerical finite part, numerical original-cutoff convergence or unnormalized continuum vacuum is supplied.

after.title: Connected two-current trees admit every fixed normal order
after.statement: Connected two-current classical-action-Hessian trees at bare order \(\chi\) have a prepared local/forward extension for every fixed pair of normal and holomorphic orders. Complete finite-upper-time moments subtract all proper one-root and two-root clusters, disjoint products and overlapping alternatives. The resolved and coincident strong limits agree with error \(O(\delta(1+|\log\delta|)^B)\), \(\delta=\sqrt\epsilon\).
hypotheses: Incoming derivatives precede zero-height restriction. Tangential roots are \(o\pm\delta\xi/2\), with \(\xi\) in a fixed compact set and \(0<L_0\le L\le L_1<\infty\).
Fix every field, component, derivative and polynomial normal-growth stage on the original completed projective joint tests; constants may depend on those stages.
Overlaps wholly inside one small rooted component remain alternative terms of its complete smaller forest. Only nested or disjoint clusters occur together.
Normal derivatives act on retained ambient extension data. Unary wheels, zero-vertex scalar pairs, arbitrary independent heights, prescribed-normalization equality and all-arity closure are separate.

after.title: Unary current loops and their ordered products admit all fixed normal orders
after.statement: Unary one-loop current factors have strong prepared extensions at every fixed normal and holomorphic order. Odd normal orders of a current zero-form vanish at positive cutoff; even orders retain their full finite-upper-time moments. Classical factors use the root degree \(2+m+j\), where \(m,j\) are the incoming normal and holomorphic orders, including odd scalar responses. Their graded order-one products converge with both double-subtraction terms retained.
hypotheses: Use bare \(\chi=-\hbar\), independent fixed \(\kappa\), fixed field/component stages, common positive cutoff and compact positive upper-time intervals.
The classical root-degree and scalar-edge estimates apply at every fixed incoming normal order.
An inert ghost carries the complete normal/holomorphic Leibniz sum, so an odd total normal order of a ghost composite need not vanish.
The nonzero rescaled even-order \(h\)-row witness concerns the raw leading term; it does not assert a nonzero renormalized finite part for every row.
Only the specified finite linear tail/forward words and compact tangential root resolutions are included; arbitrary independent-height or normalization comparisons remain separate.

after.title: Mixed current primitives extend across boundary and interior collisions
after.statement: The ordinary and first-plus-normal \(u,h\) one-vertex matrices, with their actual tree-dressed outgoing fields, admit finite current records and strong collision extensions. The boundary difference is \(O(a(1+|\log a|)^2)\), uniformly in all independent height, separation and common-cutoff ratios. At each fixed mean height \(m>0\), the interior difference is \(O(C_m b(1+|\log b|))\), uniformly in \(b/\sqrt\epsilon\).
hypotheses: Work in \(a\le a_0<\min(1,\sqrt{L_0}/16)\), with \(L\in[L_0,L_1]\subset(0,\infty)\), bare order \(\chi\) and fixed field, test and holomorphic-jet stages.

The boundary record retains the exact heated degree-one layer; the interior direct diagonal also uses its moving Taylor record. Divergent moments keep the actual cutoff-dependent legs and finite \(L\).
The centered subtraction gives the same boundary finite part of this primitive. Its separate interior current power is zero at the boundary itself.
The result covers one-vertex ordinary/first-normal rows, including their ordered \(h,s\) spectator extensions; it does not prove higher incoming normals or higher connected cores.

after.title: The independent-height source comparison retains a spatial Poisson contact
after.statement: At separated roots, the original common-cutoff source equals the zero-lower-cutoff interior kernel on the same original residuals plus its explicit spatial Poisson layer and an \(O(\delta b^{-j-k-6})\) error. The layer has bound \(O(a(1+|\log a|))\); its spatial kernel has boundary-first value \(\Pi_{<\epsilon}(0,\cdot)=\pi\delta_0\). Its opposite mixed-current signs and every spectator derivative remain.
hypotheses: These source and layer estimates require \(0<\delta=\sqrt\epsilon\le b/8\), in the fixed collar. For root heights \(r_\pm\ge0\) and tangential separation \(d\), \(a^2=(r_++r_-)^2+2|d|^2\) and \(b^2=(r_+-r_-)^2+2|d|^2\); \(j,k\) are the fixed incoming holomorphic orders. This restriction is not imposed on the separate all-ratio boundary extension.

With \(g_s(v)=(4\pi s)^{-1/2}e^{-v^2/(4s)}\) and \(h_s(z)=(2\pi s)^{-1}e^{-|z|^2/(2s)}\), the spatial kernel is \(\Pi_{<\epsilon}(r,z)=\pi r\int_0^\epsilon g_s(r)h_s(z)\,ds/s\). Its boundary-first value \(\pi\delta_0\) is assigned separately; it is not obtained by substituting \(r=0\) inside the integrand.

For a root \(q=(r,o)\), the zero-lower finite-upper-time responses are \(\Phi_q=2\pi\partial_z\int_0^L\operatorname{erfc}((t+r)/(2\sqrt s))h_s(z-o)\,ds\) and \(R_{t,q}=-2\pi\partial_z\int_0^L[g_s(t-r)+g_s(t+r)]h_s(z-o)\,ds\). The Poisson factor is centred at the plus root and these responses at the minus root; their products are evaluated at the boundary. At an opposing boundary root, both \(\Pi_{<\epsilon}R_t\) and \(\Pi_{<\epsilon}\partial_z\Phi\) are signed distributions defined by tangential derivative transfer.
Each homogeneous row keeps its assigned original residual order. A scalar error-function mass alone does not specify the contact.
The primitive does not absorb scalar source-normal-product, PBW or reassociation contacts and does not establish a grouped Ward identity.

after.title: The ordered antighost scalar companion has a fixed negative sign
after.statement: The full one-vertex ordered \(b,j_A\) kernel is \(\frac{\chi}{\pi}\int[-\Phi_+\rho_-(j_{[E,A]})-\Phi_+(2S_{uA}H_{tb}-S_{hA}F_{tb})]\,dX\), with \(S=-P_z\Phi_-\). Reversing the second sign changes a nonzero finite functional, detected on a smooth compact interior test even after cutoff removal. Vanishing critical scalar moments do not remove that functional.
hypotheses: Use the actual forms-left component action, left odd derivative and root-first pairing \(C(b_0,c_0)=-\Phi\), at common \(0<\epsilon<L\). The ordered roots are \(b(o_+)\) and \(j_A(o_-)\), where \(A\in\{E,H,F\}\), and \(\chi=-\hbar\).

For a bulk point \(X=(t,z)\) and boundary root \(o\), set \(g_s(t)=(4\pi s)^{-1/2}e^{-t^2/(4s)}\), \(h_s(z)=(2\pi s)^{-1}e^{-|z|^2/(2s)}\), and \(\Phi(X,o)=2\pi\partial_z\int_\epsilon^L\operatorname{erfc}(t/(2\sqrt s))h_s(z-o)\,ds\). The subscript \(\pm\) evaluates a response at \(o_\pm\).

The current cross responses are \(r_t(X,o)=-4\pi\partial_z\int_\epsilon^L g_s(t)h_s(z-o)\,ds\) and \(r_b(X,o)=2\pi\partial_t\int_\epsilon^L g_s(t)h_s(z-o)\,ds\). Put \(\rho_-(v)=v_t r_{b,-}-v_b r_{t,-}\); \(H=\eta_h\), \(F=\eta_f\), and component \(b\) denotes \(d\bar z\).

In row order \((u,h,f)\) and current column order \((E,H,F)\), \(P_z=\begin{pmatrix}0&2&\kappa\partial_z\\-2&2\kappa\partial_z&0\\\kappa\partial_z&0&0\end{pmatrix}\), and \(S_{iA}=-P_z^{iA}\Phi_-\). The level \(\kappa\) is fixed independently of \(\chi\).

For undivided incoming holomorphic orders \(j,k\ge0\), \(\lambda_{j,k}(\epsilon,L)=\frac4\pi\int_\epsilon^L\int_\epsilon^L s^{k+1/2}v^{j+1/2}(s+v)^{-j-k-3}\,ds\,dv\). The first-normal local coefficients are \(-\chi\lambda_{j,k}\partial^{j+k+1}u_t/2\) and \(+\chi\lambda_{j,k}\partial^{j+k+1}h_t/4\).

For two full operations differing by \(\Delta\), the residual difference is \(Q\Delta-\Delta q\), including source precomposition, relative, action and BV terms. No general vanishing or blanket equivalence of the resulting operations follows.

after.title: Boundary first-normal insertion covers the full finite affine–ghost source
after.statement: Every fixed finite state in the universal \(e,h,f,b,c\) source has prepared ordinary and indicated first-normal insertions through bare orders zero and one. The construction includes the nonzero normal-antighost unary loop, all ordered pair classes, actual PBW/source contacts and the full quantum source differential. It has strong boundary limits, exact affine heat transport and a complete grouped Ward residual.
hypotheses: Fix the polarized source words and separate normal-contact extensions. One height derivative is taken before zero-height restriction; tangential ratios and positive running scales remain in compact sets.
Use finite source, holomorphic-jet, physical field and component stages on the original joint tests; source stages include their actual \(q\)-images.
Retain \(W^1J^0\), the complete left-ordered master covariance, lower and upper BV terms, relative ghost symbols and every source-precomposition term.

The actual finite PBW stress state is included as an input. Identification with an independently prescribed physical stress target, residual vanishing and higher quantum/normal orders remain separate.

after.title: Every colour with an actual normal form component gives the projection invariant
after.statement: Finite component tensors containing an actual \(dt\) field slot form a common invariant for the prescribed normalized homotopies and complete classical action dressing. The finite PBW conversion is oriented as \(G=J^{\mathrm{UV}}-J^R=\chi T^0Z^{\beta(R)}\pmod{\chi^2}\). Its fixed normal projections and full Hom differential satisfy \(P_A G=P_A\delta G=0\pmod{\chi^2}\). All fixed ordered comparison cells retain their \(\delta G\) companions.
hypotheses: Here \(J^{\mathrm{UV}}\) and \(J^R\) are the ultraviolet-logarithm and full reference-moment insertions at reference scale \(R>0\), with identical source PBW and contact-extension data. \(T^0\) is the complete classical insertion. \(Z^{\beta(R)}\) is the complete marked coincident pair polynomial, including current and antighost terms, with coefficients \(\beta_{j,k}(R)\) given by the finite limits of full reference moments minus their ultraviolet logarithms. Every unconsumed letter and its ordered jet Leibniz terms remain.
The invariant includes every internal colour, the \(u_t,h_t\) outputs and arbitrary admitted ghost spectators. A normal derivative of a zero-form is not a \(dt\) component.

For a fixed action-corrected normal contraction \(A\), \(P_A\) is its normal projection and \(H_A\) its classical homotopy. The symbol \(\delta\) denotes the full Hom differential, with recipient action and source-precomposition terms. Put \(K_A=H_AG\) and \(K_{BA}=H_BH_AG\). Then \(G=\delta K_A+H_A\delta G\) and \(K_A-K_B=\delta K_{BA}-H_BH_A\delta G\); no homotopies are commuted.

Continuity is for every fixed finite word and stage with its finite derivative/normal-weight cost. Projected zero is not closedness, full source contractibility or an exhaustive correction-quotient theorem.

after.title: The first Ward identity descends through unmarked composition
after.statement: For actual degree-zero unmarked polynomial \(W,J\) currents, the composition defect \(B(U,V)=D_{\mathscr N}(U\star V)-(D_{\mathscr N}U)\star V-U\star(D_{\mathscr N}V)\) is a well-defined contact current on the cross complex sheets. It descends through equality in the actual source images. Its unit, symmetry and associativity cocycle identities give the complete first finite Ward formula: each binary contact is composed with the entire spectator operation. The total differential differentiates the native family, including \(D_{\mathscr N}W=-p\). All finite holomorphic derivatives act on the whole moving coefficient family.
hypotheses: Work on finite labelled configurations in \(\mathbb R_t\times\mathbb C_z\). The external mixed differential is \(D_{\rm ext}=d_t+\bar\partial_z\), denoted \(D\) in scalar-kernel formulas. The actual total native differential is \(D_{\mathscr N}=D_{\rm ext}+Q+\delta\), with external forms placed on the left. Smooth native \(W,J,p\) coefficient families over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]\) retain all surviving particle sectors.

Graph size, pole orders, particle number, field degree and native jets are finite. Use the specified canonical whole-current extension in the selected subcritical tame class, with common local carriers, collars and test-order bounds on parameter compacts.
Products of admitted images use disjoint labelled blocks and retain their full labelled parameter spaces. Bounds are on finite presentation stages and their actual image bornology.
The inputs have no initial height gates. The assertion computes the first differential and binary composition defect; it does not assert closure under every later differential of a marked output.

after.title: Diamond contacts retain their complete possible holomorphic jets
after.statement: For the five-edge diamond with positive pole orders and total pole order \(M\), the differential is an origin-supported combination of holomorphic delta jets of order \(M-3\). In the shared-edge family \((s,1,1,1,1)\), the coefficient of \(\partial_u^{s-1}\partial_v\partial_w\Omega\) in \(DK^{(s)}\) is \((-1)^{s+1}/[4(2s+1)(s-1)!]\), where \(K^{(s)}=K_{s,1,1,1,1}\) and \(\Omega=C_1(a)\wedge C_1(b)\wedge C_1(c)\). Its nonzero normal order is exactly \(s+1\). The complete first jets satisfy \(DX=-\Theta/20\) and \(DY=DZ=-\Theta/30\). A native input with five \(p\) and five \(J\) fields realizes the vacuum coefficient \(-8\hbar^5Y\), whose differential is \(4\hbar^5\Theta/15\), while retaining the particle sectors \(10,8,6,4,2,0\).
hypotheses: Work on finite labelled configurations in \(\mathbb R_t\times\mathbb C_z\), with mixed differential \(D=d_t+\bar\partial_z\), smooth native \(W,J,p\) coefficient families over \(\mathbb C[\hbar]\), and all surviving particle sectors.

Graph size, pole orders, particle number, field degree and native jets are finite. Use the specified canonical whole-current extension in the selected subcritical tame class, with common local carriers, collars and test-order bounds on parameter compacts.

stages.label: One nilpotent current has an exact unbounded torsion comparison
stages.description: For \(x=at\) with nonzero ad-nilpotent \(a\), smooth Ore localization \(L_x\) is exact and \(i_xR\Gamma_xM\simeq\operatorname{fib}(M\to L_xM)\) on every ordinary unbounded smooth complex. The inclusion of the derived \(x\)-torsion category is fully faithful, with exactly \(x\)-torsion cohomology as image.

stages.label: A finite nilpotent basis detects joint torsion
stages.description: A nilpotent basis \(a_i\) of \(\mathfrak g\), with \(x_i=a_it\), gives \(\mathcal T_I=\bigcap_i\ker L_{x_i}\) and \(D_I=\bigcap_i\ker DL_{x_i}\). These exact detectors characterize joint torsion and its cohomological category.

stages.label: The single-current localizations do not preserve each other’s torsion
stages.description: At every affine \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) level, an explicit smooth module is \(ft\)-torsion while its localization at \(et\) is not. Thus iterating the single-current detectors is not automatically a construction of joint derived torsion.

stages.label: Positive-current torsion is stable under injective envelopes
stages.description: The smooth positive-current category is locally noetherian, and joint augmentation torsion is stable under injective envelopes. Finite nilpotent Rees algebras and the resulting Artin–Rees statement give the actual stability theorem on every smooth cyclic module.

stages.label: Actual derived torsion commutes with positive-current restriction
stages.description: Exact induction on the smooth and torsion categories yields \(\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal T}R\Gamma_A\simeq R\Gamma_{\mathfrak n}\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal S}\) on every ordinary unbounded complex, with the actual units and counits. Restriction is conservative; every torsion affine module is \(\Gamma_A\)-acyclic, so \(\Gamma_A\) is weakly stable.

stages.label: Positive-current derived torsion has infinite cohomological dimension
stages.description: For \(R_N=U(\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n_N)\) with its inflated regular action, the first nonzero derived torsion lies in degree \(d_N=(N-1)\dim\mathfrak g\). Its invariant line has energy \(\Delta_N=\dim(\mathfrak g)N(N-1)/2\). These degrees are unbounded.

stages.label: Positive-current derived torsion fails to preserve a countable coproduct
stages.description: For the shifted regular quotients \(R_N[d_N]\), the actual comparison \(\bigoplus_N R\Gamma(R_N[d_N])\to R\Gamma(\bigoplus_N R_N[d_N])\) has a nonzero degree-zero defect containing \(\mathbb C^{\mathbb N}/\mathbb C^{(\mathbb N)}\). An actual acyclic complex of injectives \(K\) realizes the defect: \(R\Gamma K=0\) but termwise \(\Gamma K\) is not acyclic.

stages.label: The unrestricted torsion-cohomology comparison
stages.description: The full equality \(D_I=C_W\) is equivalent to \(D_I\cap\ker(\mathbf R\Gamma_I)=0\). The cellularization theorem isolates this residual and proves it has no nonzero bounded-below objects, but does not prove that it vanishes on all unbounded objects.

stages.label: Comparing intrinsic and ambient torsion categories
stages.description: Full faithfulness and an essential-image description for \(\operatorname{D}(T)\to\operatorname{D}(\operatorname{Sm}(A))\) remain outside these results. The operators \(i\mathbf R\Gamma_I\) and \(\operatorname{Cell}_I\) are not identified by the proof; neither their equality nor their inequality is established.

after.title: A bare exterior E3 algebra has no coupling parameter
after.text:
A strictly unital \(E_3\)-algebra over \(\mathbb C\) with cohomology \(\Lambda(x_3)\), \(|x_3|=3\), is unique up to equivalence at the level of its bare \(E_3\) structure. That structure alone therefore supplies no varying coupling scalar. A filtration, mixed action, retained translation or central-charge class, marked comparison, or braided category is additional data.

Scope: This is single-generator exterior rigidity. It is not a rigidity theorem for arbitrary simple affine cohomology, and uniqueness does not construct an enhancement on a separately prescribed object. Rank-one coefficient Koszul comparisons retain their specified unipotent sector and separate charge grading; no full all-charge braided equivalence follows from bare formality.

# Ordered composition, duality and quantum states

The programme has explicit field algebras, derived module comparisons, geometric operation systems and analytic sewings. Several are complete theories on their stated domains. The frontier includes further algebraic calculations and categorical classifications, as well as comparisons with independently defined bulk observables, defects and prepared states. Each comparison must preserve the operations that make its objects useful: multiplication, collision, exchange, units, source dependence and higher homotopies.

The Heisenberg current gives a small example of why the data matter. At nonzero level its double pole is a nonzero multiple of the vacuum. A unital map of fields to scalars would have to preserve that pole, while scalar fields have no singular product. The vacuum exists without a scalar augmentation. Elsewhere, the empty configuration, an occupied vacuum, a pointing and a physical cap are also distinct objects. A comparison that preserves one need not supply the others.

Associative chiral Koszul duality has a complete foundation on ordered configurations. On a smooth separated finite-type curve over a characteristic-zero field, consecutive-cut bar and cobar give inverse equivalences between the specified coherent associative algebras \(A\) and counital coaugmented coalgebras \(C\), with both \(A_0\simeq k\) and \(C_0\simeq k\). The equivalence includes mapping spaces. Reduced words have length at most the number of positions, so this theorem permits unbounded coefficient complexes. Its strong-cut restriction is a supported-section theorem; at three positions the relevant support is the nonconsecutive diagonal. This finite arity argument does not select a completion of modes or identify an independently defined continuous dual.

Universal affine and Virasoro modes have polarized curved duality with the raw central curvature retained. Their smooth and contramodule categories use specified null classes and degreewise completions; complementary levels describe a separate categorical duality. There is also a translated spectral bar theorem for strict augmented dg bialgebras with compatible locally nilpotent translation. The actual tensor comparison is an equivalence when either input lies in the thick category generated by the augmentation module. Compactness extends the equivalence to its localizing category, without making that module generate the entire derived category. Finite exterior uncurving marks have strict dg bi-Galois transport by algebraic cotensor in their marked localizations.

Geometric reconstruction is available when the input diagram is supplied. A compatible system of categories, realizations and vacua over a smooth curve, with all finite-set pullbacks, disjoint fusion, the actual empty unit and the required exclusion of collision-supported coefficient torsion, reconstructs a unital chiral algebra. Translation-equivariant data on the affine line give a vertex algebra.
